C19H23NO3,HCl,2H2O = 385.9. CAS — 76-58-4 (ethylmorphine); 125-30-4 (ethylmor- phine hydrochloride). ATC — R05DA01; S01XA06. ATC Vet — QR05DA01; QS01XA06. (ethylmorphine) Pharmacopoeias. In Chin., Eur. (see p.vii), and Jpn. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Ethylmorphine Hydrochloride). A white or almost white crystalline powder. Soluble in water and in alcohol. A 2% solution in water has a pH of 4.3 to 5.7. Protect from light. Profile Ethylmorphine hydrochloride is an opioid analgesic (p.101) and has properties similar to those of codeine (p.37). It is used mainly as a cough suppressant. It has also been used for its analgesic and antidiarrhoeal properties. It was formerly given in eye drops as a lymphagogue. Ethylmorphine free base and the camphorate and camsilate have also been used. ◊ References. 1. Aasmundstad TA, et al. Biotransformation and pharmacokinet- ics of ethylmorphine after a single oral dose. Br J Clin Pharma- col 1995; 39: 611–20. 2. Jonasson B, et al. Fatal poisonings where ethylmorphine from antitussive medications contributed to death. Int J Legal Med 1999; 112: 299–302.
